findings.issue: Iteration 10 is recorded as the hard cap, production changes were nevertheless made and published in iteration 13, and the workflow has now reached a twentieth implementer tick. This tick correctly changed only review/bookkeeping artifacts, but another implementation tick would continue violating the governing stop condition.
findings.consequence: Further implementation in this workflow would be unauthorized post-cap work without the promised bounded review cycle.
findings.correction: Stop this loop after this review, preserve the published linear history without reset/revert/force operations, and carry the product blockers into a separately authorized run.

findings.criterion: 7 and cross-cutting security — mandatory idempotency for Super Admin tenant creation
findings.issue: POST /v1/platform/tenants is replaySafe rather than idempotent. definePlatformRoute executes the handler when Idempotency-Key is absent, existing route tests prove keyless creation is accepted, and provisionTenant auto-suffixes a colliding generated slug. A lost-response keyless retry can therefore provision a second live property.
findings.consequence: One intended Super Admin action can duplicate a property, owner, inventory, policy, and audit history.
findings.correction: Require Idempotency-Key on tenant creation, update every caller/test to send one stable submission-scoped key, reject keyless requests, and test that a lost-response retry returns the original property while the UI prevents an in-flight duplicate submit.

findings.criterion: 7 and cross-cutting data integrity — atomic, recoverable platform creation/idempotency
findings.issue: The platform idempotency reservation, create_tenant call, tenant initialization transaction, and replay finalization are separate commits. There is no lease, durable operation-to-tenant identity, reconciliation, or compensation. A failure after create_tenant can leave a partial tenant and delete the reservation; a crash after the business commit but before finalization leaves status=0 permanently.
findings.consequence: Property creation can strand an unusable or partially initialized property; exact-key recovery can remain blocked while a fresh key can create a duplicate.
findings.correction: Make creation, initialization, and replay completion one transaction, or persist a unique operation-to-tenant identity with resumable phases and stale-operation recovery. Add fault-injection tests after create_tenant and after the business commit but before replay finalization, proving retries converge on one complete property.

findings.criterion: 6 and 7 — recoverable local-auth person and owner onboarding
findings.location: apps/api/src/services/people.ts:15-37; apps/api/src/services/tenants.ts:43-55; apps/api/src/http.ts:117-119,206-208; apps/api/src/routes/people.ts:194-208,300-336; apps/web/src/screens/People.tsx:249-253; apps/web/src/screens/Platform.tsx:24-36; apps/web/src/screens/Auth.tsx:65-81,103-114; apps/api/test/api.test.ts:383-395
findings.issue: Local onboarding stores only a generated password hash and returns the plaintext once, while both replay stores replace temporaryPassword with null. The local-auth UI exposes no working recovery path: forgot/reset is linked and implemented only for external auth, and a local /forgot submission falls into the login request. A lost first response therefore loses the only credential.
findings.consequence: A created tenant member, cross-property member, or new property's only owner can be unable to sign in without direct database intervention.
findings.correction: Add a recoverable expiring setup/invitation flow or authenticated credential-reset flow without storing plaintext secrets. Define replay behavior explicitly and test lost-response retries for all three creation paths through successful first local sign-in.

findings.issue: Rendered tests exercise Share/public-QR/attendant behavior and API tests separately execute two-hour expiry, HMAC rejection, and stored verify_code mismatch, but the joined rendered test starts from a fabricated token, mounts GuestPass directly, substitutes the scanner, and mocks lookup/redeem. The existing real-stack browser script issues and redeems a live pass but does not invoke Share or route through the public guest page. No recorded execution joins the complete shipped path.
findings.consequence: The exact server-issued artifact produced by the live Share control has not been shown to survive the routed guest handoff and redeem as the same valid pass.
findings.correction: In a separately authorized run, execute and record a 390x844 routed browser story from live pass issue through the real Share control, /pass#t=..., rendered QR decode, and real lookup/redeem. Assert exact token identity, default two-hour unused expiry, HMAC-field tamper rejection, and stored verify_code mismatch rejection.

findings.criterion: 3 and 4 — real camera plate scanning at check-in and check-out
findings.issue: Rendered tests replace LiveCamera with a button that emits an already-decoded plate. No recorded run executes getUserMedia, the shipped ONNX loader/decoder, a camera fixture, and responsive rendering for both flows; the existing browser script covers check-in only and has no recorded execution in this review run.
findings.consequence: Actual camera acquisition/model decoding may fail before the covered downstream field wiring, and checkout camera behavior remains unverified in the shipped stack.
findings.correction: In a separately authorized run, record 390x844 real-model fake-camera stories for check-in and checkout, including visible filled fields, checkout match/result, browser/model/fixture versions, stopped media tracks after navigation, and a clean console.

findings.criterion: 6 and 7 — complete real-stack CRUD and cross-property operations
findings.issue: The rendered suite mocks every API and completes a full lifecycle only for a unit; person is create-only, site/zone/slot coverage is incomplete, and cross-property coverage is one mocked member POST. The browser script exercises unit/site/zone/slot operations at 1280px but not complete person CRUD, second-property all-entity operations, or the regular-admin server boundary, and no recorded run establishes narrow responsive behavior.
findings.consequence: Persisted all-entity administration, representative all-entity Super Admin behavior across properties, server authorization boundaries, and narrow-screen usability remain unverified in context.
findings.correction: In a separately authorized run, execute create/read/edit/delete-or-retire for person, site/building, unit, and slot through the real routed UI/API at a narrow viewport. Repeat representative all-entity operations in a second property as Super Admin and prove regular-admin server denial.
